q0063: Keeping records for a required period (legal or regulatory) = data retention. A legal hold overrides normal retention and deletion schedules once litigation starts.
q0064: Secure zones + one policy enforced everywhere + 'never trust, always verify' = Zero Trust (policy engine, policy administrator, policy enforcement points).
q0065: Detect or track changes to files and system settings = FIM (file integrity monitoring), which compares hashes against a known-good baseline.
q0066: Anything set up before an incident (roles, contact lists, tools, playbooks, training) belongs to the preparation phase.
q0067: Outsourced disposal → ask for a certificate of destruction or sanitization, as proof and for the audit trail.
q0068: Only authorized people get in = something that authenticates (badge) + something that stops tailgating (access control vestibule). Cameras and sign-in sheets only record.
q0069: Data roles: subject = the person the data is about; owner = accountable leader; controller = decides why and how; processor = handles it for the controller; custodian = protects it daily.
q0070: The attacker infects a site the victims already trust and visit (an industry blog or forum) = watering-hole attack.
q0071: Reading logs after an attack = detective control. Restoring from backup = corrective.
q0072: Response times, uptime percentages and penalties = SLA. MOU/MOA = intent and cooperation; SOW = project deliverables.
q0073: To investigate what an attacker actually sent (the payloads), you need full packet capture. NetFlow only has metadata: who, when and how much.
q0074: Any number like 99.99% uptime or a four-hour response time lives in the SLA.
q0075: Modifying a phone's OS to remove its restrictions = jailbreaking (iOS) or rooting (Android). Installing apps from outside the store = side loading.
q0076: Stop one insider slipping in malicious code = peer review and approval (separation of duties for code). Scanners find bugs, not intent.
q0077: Scripts that chain steps across systems to save time and remove human error = automation and orchestration.
q0078: The fastest fix for too-broad access to files and folders = change the ACLs (permissions).
q0079: Ransomware-as-a-service, extortion and profit = organized crime. Politics = hacktivist; espionage = nation-state.
q0080: End-of-life = no more patches. The security implication is patch availability: known vulnerabilities stay open.
q0081: Government or other sensitive project data → confidential and restricted. Public = no harm if disclosed; private = personal information.
q0082: The scanner flags a risk but your own check shows it is mitigated another way → compensating controls exist, not a false positive.
q0083: Secure remote access into a network = VPN, and IPSec is the classic VPN protocol suite. EAP authenticates, DHCP hands out addresses, NAT translates them.
q0084: A planned window for changes with minimal business impact = scheduled downtime (a maintenance window).
q0085: Watching every host for unauthorized changes and software → an agent on every endpoint (endpoint management or EDR). Network tools cannot see inside hosts.
q0086: A phone call impersonating an executive to get data or money = social engineering (vishing). Whaling targets the executives themselves.
q0087: Improve the IR process without touching production = tabletop exercise. Failover and replication test infrastructure, not the process.
q0088: Real-time revocation check = OCSP (stapling makes it faster). CRL = the downloadable list of revoked certificates. CSR = a request for a new certificate.
q0089: A legacy or IoT device with no quick patch → segment it. Segmentation is the fast mitigation; replacement is the slow one.
q0090: Stolen laptop, lost drive, 'data at rest' → encryption at rest (full disk encryption).
q0091: Constantly changing, scaling, frequent releases → containers (or serverless). Embedded systems, RTOS and SCADA are built to stay the same.
q0092: Remote desktop exposed to the internet → put it behind a VPN, with the jump server inside the firewall. Changing the port is only obscurity.
